title: Prototyping in Unreal 5.8 looking for honest feedback for my racing game idea
author: jaykrown
selftext:
My idea is to race a vehicle that has very little friction powered by rocket thrusters. You slide around thrust vectoring along slopes to get the fastest times. 

I received a lot of feedback about how the flying transformer idea was too complex. So I leaned my inspiration back towards old school lords of dogtown style bowl. I don't think this will be the actual goal to create like a skateboarding game, but I think it shows how this could be a cool form of racing. 

Any suggestions/feedback is great appreciated, thank you!

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: Aw, man now I want a skateboarding racing game.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: There are quite a few of those already which use similar feeling controls with proper wheel friction I think. The idea to have it be thrust vectored makes it feel a bit different, to get that best feeling of like sliding while drifting, combining drift racing with bowl skateboarding.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body: why can't the skateboarders be on thrust vectored boards? Some kind of futuristic skateboarding racing game with some sick tricks for good measure

comments.author: freqCake
comments.body: Its all about how good the controls feel. With thrust vectoring you risk spinning out and feeling a lot of undearsteer or oversteer. So the controls have to feel really solid.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Not sure what you mean with "spinning out" in the context of a near zero friction thrust vectoring racer? I think leaning towards the thrusting being very powerful is probably for the best. Track design will also be a major factor, but I think using Unreal 5.8 will make that a lot easier, not sure.

replies.author: freqCake
replies.body: I mean when it spins sideways it should be easy to recover so that your thrust is in the direction you are facing again or else it just kind of feels like you are losing speed and cant fix it.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: That makes sense. In this game idea, being sideways has no extra impact on losing speed. You can be facing completely backwards and still slide in your direction of momentum, where thrust vectoring is the only thing impacting your acceleration aside from very subtle friction.

comments.author: Tiny_Flatworm4726
comments.body: Dude someone si going to steal this for sure

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: I don't care I'll still be developing it. Please support me and not someone who steals it, I'll make sure to make it better than they can!

replies.author: Tiny_Flatworm4726
replies.body: Nice man, great attitute - look at "Get to work" I think something like that style of gameplay would suit this

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thanks, that game looks awesome I appreciate you mentioning it. I also got sliprace dot com just to make sure I have that reserved name for it.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thank you, if you have any suggestions/feedback feel free to let me know, I'm open to any new ideas.
